newsitem.title: INDIA: India's CRISIL says reaffirms ICICI's 'AAA' rating.
newsitem.headline: India's CRISIL says reaffirms ICICI's 'AAA' rating.

text.p: India's leading credit rating agency, CRISIL, said it reaffirmed its 'AAA' ratings of ICICI following the company's plans to merge with SCICI Ltd, another term lending institution.
It said in a statement it was reaffirming its 'AAA" ratings of SCICI.
An AAA ratings indicates highest safety.

CRISIL (The Credit Rating Information Service of India) said following the merger, the capital adequacy of ICICI (Industrial Credit & Investment Corporation of India Ltd) is expected to improve to around 13 percent while the asset base of the merged entity would be 33.43 billion rupees as at September 30, 1996.
Last week ICICI said boards of both institutions would recommend to shareholders a merger of their activities with effect from April 1, 1996.
In New York, Moody's Investors Service said on Monday it affirmed its long term debt ratings of Baa3 for ICICI and SCICI Ltd.
The CRISIL statement said it was reaffirming its 'AAA' ratings for ICICI's four bond issues and a certificates of deposit programme.
